content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter part of the forecast, particularly when true values show upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true values by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast window.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts overshoot and then gradually correct, but often remain too high for 2–4 days.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward lower values in the middle of the forecast, especially when true values are trending upward.
- Model fails to capture the full magnitude of recent price corrections, underestimating the depth of mean reversion.
- Forecasts are overly smooth, missing short-term volatility and sudden reversals in the last 5–7 days.
- Model tends to overcorrect after a downward correction, leading to premature recovery signals.
